question:
Real numbers \(x,\) \(y,\) and \(z\) satisfy the inequalities

\[0 \lt x \lt 1, \quad -1 \lt y \lt 0,\] and \[1 \lt z \lt 2.\]

Which of the following numbers is necessarily positive?
solution:
The lower bounds for \(y\) and \(z\) add to zero. Since \(y>-1\) and \(z>1\), adding these inequalities gives
\[
y+z>(-1)+1=0.
\]
Thus choice E is positive for every allowed triple.

For the other choices, take \(x=\frac18\), \(y=-\frac14\), and \(z=\frac32\), which satisfy all the given bounds. Then
\[
\begin{aligned}
\text{A: }y+x^2&=-\frac14+\frac1{64}=-\frac{15}{64},\\
\text{B: }y+xz&=-\frac14+\frac3{16}=-\frac1{16},\\
\text{C: }y+y^2&=-\frac14+\frac1{16}=-\frac3{16},\\
\text{D: }y+2y^2&=-\frac14+\frac2{16}=-\frac18.
\end{aligned}
\]
All four are negative in this example, so none is necessarily positive. The answer is \(\boxed{y+z}\), choice \(\text{E}\).
